units.title: Europe and USA in the Interwar Period

lessons.title: Europe and USA in the Interwar Period

cards.title: Focus question: What does it mean by interwar period?
body: The term “interwar” refers to the period that stretches from the end of the First World War in 1919 to the beginning of the Second World War in 1939.
The interwar period was characterized by difficult economic problems and emergence of dictatorial regimes in Italy, Germany, Russia, and Eastern Europe.
Elsewhere in Africa, the Middle East, Asia and Latin America (South America), the interwar period was characterized by the rise of nationalism and national movements.

cards.title: Efforts for Peace and Security
body: The peace settlement at the end of World War I had sought to bring peace among the warring states. It created the League of Nations to guarantee collective peace and security.

From the beginning, however, the peace settlement left many states unhappy. Eastern Europe was beset by border disputes and many Germans felt bitter about the Treaty of Versailles and vowed to revise it.
Some of the weakness of the league of nations was:
The absence of powerful countries like USA, JAPAN, ITALY and LATER GERMANY also withdraw.
Lack of army made the league unable to implement its decisions.
Some of the events that the league of nations failed to stop include:
Failed to stop border dispute in Eastern Europe.
Failed to stop japan invasion of china territory called Manchuria in 1931.
Failed Germany invasion of Poland and Czechoslovakia in 1939 and 1938 respectively.
Failed to stop Italian invasion of Ethiopia in 1936. And other more.

cards.title: The Question of Reparation
body: Between 1919 and 1924, France demanded a strict enforcement of the Treaty of Versailles. It pressured Germany to pay the reparations agreed in the Treaty. In April 1921, the Allied Reparations Commission decided that Germany pay 132 billion German Marks (33 billion U.S. dollars), payable in annual installment of 2.5million Marks. Germany made its first payment in 1921.

By the following year, however, the German government announced that it was unable to pay any more because of financial problems. France was outraged and sent troops to occupy the Ruhr Valley, Germany’s main industrial and mining center. As a result, German workers went on strike, and their government paid them salaries by printing more paper money. Printing more paper money resulted in higher inflation in Germany.

The economic problems in Germany created unemployment, hyperinflation, loss of life time savings and etc. Strikes by German workers of the Ruhr and British and American protests against the occupation forced France to withdraw from the Ruhr Valley. In August 1924, an international commission produced a new plan for reparations. This new plan was known as the Dawes Plan, after the American banker who chaired the commission. The plan had two objectives:
Reduce the net payment Germany must pay annually based on its ability.
And give 200 million $ for recovery European and Germany economy.
A brief period of European prosperity followed, but it only lasted from 1924 to 1929.

cards.title: The Great Depression
body: A depression is a period of low economic activity and rising unemployment. It was start in 1920s and throughout 1930s,the economies of western countries collapsed. The great depression had big negative consequences on the social, economic, and political conditions of western countries It devastated public morale and led to the rise and strengthening of extreme political parties. The fundamental cause of the depression can be found in the inherent problems of capitalist economic system.
Uneven distribution of land and resource.
Unregulated free market.
The serious decline of economy.

The full United states stock market.1924s the U,S stock market gave to Germany loan under the Dawns plan. Germany needed the US loan to pay reparations to France and Great Britain. In October 1929, the US stock market crushed and the prices of stock collapsed.

In fear US investors withdrew even more money from Germany and other European markets. This withdrew even more money from Germany and other European market. As a result, industrial production declined, and unemployment rose.

cards.title: EFFECTS OF GERAT DEPRESSTION
body: Unemployment: During 1932,the worst year of depression, nearly one British worker in every four hours unemployed. About six million Germans or roughly 40% German labor force were out of work. Millions of Americans were left without adequate food, shelter, and clothing. However few people died from starvation.

Social changes: The economic crises had also affected the roles of men and women. Women able to get low paying jobs as servants, house cleaners and laundresses while many men remained unemployed, either begging on the streets rates or staying at home to do household tasks.

Political changes: the great depression also increased government activity in the economy. Another effect is the renewed interest in communism. Finally, the great depression led many people to join extreme parties such as the Nazis in Germany and the Fascist party in Italy.

lessons.title: Interwar Political Developments in Europe and U.S.A

cards.title: 1. EUROPE
body: In a number of European countries, women were allowed to vote. But countries such as France, Italy, and Switzerland did not allow women to vote. (Women gained the right to vote in1944 in France, in 1945 in Italy, and 1971 in Switzerland.)
In the 1920s, Europe seemed to be returning to normalcy. However, this was not an easy process.

cards.title: I.Germany
body: The Weimar Republic faced many problems from the beginning. One of the problems was the economy.
It pushed many of Germany’s middle class, like teachers and civil servants, toward political parties that were opposed to the Weimar Republic.
As a result of the Great Depression, about four and half million Germans became unemployed in 1930.
The depression created fear and insecurity among Germans and encouraged the rise of extremist parties like the Nazi.

cards.title: II. France
body: After the defeat of Germany in WWI, France became the strongest power in Europe.
However, France, too, suffered financial problems after the war.
France had a relatively stronger economy than other countries; it did not suffer the full impacts of the Great Depression until 1932.
The economic decline then led to political crises in the country. Between 1932 and 1933 only, six governments were formed as the country passed through political chaos.
Finally, in June 1936, a coalition of leftist parties formed a government known as the Popular Front government.
The Popular Front government gave French workers
The right to collective bargaining, i.e., the right of workers’ unions to negotiate with employers over wages and working hours.
In addition, the government fixed working hours to a 40-hour workweek in industry and granted two-week annual paid vacation to workers.

cards.title: III.Great Britain
body: Britain had lost many markets for its industrial products. In many places, the United States and Japan replaced Great Britain as the main exporters of industrial products.
British industries declined and the rate of unemployment increased. In 1921, two million Britons were unemployed.
Moreover, the return of large numbers of soldiers from the war pushed up prices and drove down wages.
As the British economy worsened, the conservative government broke apart. In 1924, the first labor government came to power promising to improve the conditions of British workers.
But, the labor government also failed to fulfill the needs of British workers. Therefore, after only one year in power, the labor government was brought down by a series of workers’ strikes in 1925.

The Labor party was elected in 1929 in coalition with the Liberal party. The coalition tried to introduce a program of social welfare and full employment. But before it started to implement its policies, the Great Depression began.
The depression hit Britain hard. Unemployment rose to 2.5 million within a year and to 3 million by the beginning of 1933. The Labor prime minister was forced to resign in 1931.

cards.title: The United States
body: Same as the powerful countries USA was faced unemployment, any suffered homelessness and starvation.
Under such terrible circumstances, a Democratic candidate named Franklin Delano Roosevelt won a landslide victory in the 1932 presidential election.
Roosevelt introduced a new policy of active government intervention in the economy known as the New Deal.
The policy of New Deal was aimed at creating recovery and reform. It also included relief for the homeless and destitute.

cards.title: Focus question
body: Have you ever heard of dictatorships? Explain what you understand by dictatorships?

In the 1930s, dictatorial or totalitarian regimes emerged in eastern and central Europe and elsewhere. A dictatorial or totalitarian government is a government that tries to control the political, economic, social, intellectual, and cultural lives of its citizens.

cards.title: Totalitarian governments have many characteristics in common. Some of them are
body: They want total obedience from their citizens and try to win popular support through massive propaganda.
They are led by a single leader and a political party.
They are opposed to individual freedoms and use security agencies to brutally suppress opponents.

cards.title: Soviet Russia – Cause for the rise of dictatorial regime in Russia
body: *civil war of 1918-1921
*severe drought that kills 5 million in 1920-23

cards.title: Lenin reforms include
body: *Many economic reforms in 1922.
* He created the USSR in 1923.
*Lenin died in 1924.

cards.title: Post Lenin situation
body: *struggle for power started among comrades
(The two primary rivalry was between Joseph Stalin the leader of USSR and Leo Trotsky)

cards.title: Joseph Stalin reforms
body: *He established powerful dictatorship
*In 1928 launched the 5 years plan. The five years plan was to transform USSR to industrial power.
The five year plan include for the collectivization of agriculture. Collectivization was a system in which private farms were eliminated.
Instead, the government owned all of the land, while the peasants worked it.
Millions of peasants resisted Stalin’s plan for collectivization by hoarding their crops and slaughtering their livestock.
Stalin’s government responded by imprisoning and killing millions of peasants.
*However Russia industrial power increased and illiteracy decreased
-Thus while the other European suffered the great depression Russia witnessed economic boom.

cards.title: Eastern Europe
body: By the end of 1920s and the beginning of 1930s, most of these countries adopted dictatorial regimes. Czechoslovakia was an exception; it continued to be a democratic.

cards.title: Iberian Peninsula (Spain and Portugal)
body: In Spain, the military led by General Francisco Franco revolted against the Republican government in 1936. As a result, the country entered into a brutal and bloody civil war between 1936 and 1939.The Spanish civil war was fought between two groups. The republicans and the military general Francisco Franco group.
The Spanish civil war ended when Franco’s forces defeated the Republicans in 1939.
Thereafter, Franco established a dictatorial government which lasted until 1975.

Similarly in Portugal, the Republican government was replaced by a military dictatorship in 1926. By the early 1930s, the Portuguese dictatorship was led by a man named Antonio Salazar. Salazar ruled Portugal for forty years.

lessons.title: Cultural Developments of the Interwar Period

cards.title: 1. Mass Culture: Radio and Movies
body: Some of the most important technological innovations that influenced the post First World War cultural developments were the:
Invention of radios and movie cameras.
Radio was invented by an Italian electrical engineer, Guglielmo Marconi, at the end of the 19th century.
On the other hand, movies (motion pictures) emerged in the 1890s. Shortly before WWI, full length movies began to emerge. After the end of WWI, cinema became a popular form of mass entertainment.

cards.title: 2. Mass Leisure in Europe
body: After WWI, the eight-hour workday became the normal practice for many office and factory workers in Europe.
This gave long free hours to many people. As a result, leisure activities; such as sporting events, travels, concerts, operas, and films, became common.
Travelling was made much easier by the production of trains, buses and cars. Thus, travelling became widespread pastime for many Europeans.

cards.title: 3. Artistic and Literary Developments
body: Most of the inter war period literary artistic works were based or meant to explain the misery created by the WW1 some of the works were:
In painting, two movements known as Dada and Surrealism emerged.
Dadaism was an artistic movement that was established by artists who believed that life has no purpose and meaning.
Surrealism was an artistic movement created by artists who tried to portray fantasies, dreams, and nightmares.
One of the most important post WWI writers was James Joyce. Joyce’s most famous book is the Ulysses.
Ulysses tells the story of one day in the life of ordinary people in Dublin by following the flow of their inner thoughts.
